name: 100BANCH
card: Where 100 projects led by under-35s experiment in Shibuya
title: 100BANCH — a three-storey lab in Shibuya where 100 projects take shape
lead: About a five-minute walk from Shibuya Station stands 100BANCH, a three-storey building opened on 7 July 2017 to mark Panasonic's 100th anniversary. It calls itself a lab where 100 projects are always on the move: a test kitchen on the ground floor, a garage for projects led by people under 35 on the second, and an event space for about 100 people on the third. Everything below is based on the official website.
hero_cap: A three-storey lab open to the streets of Shibuya
concept: Young energy, free of convention, for a richer world 100 years from now

100BANCH was born to celebrate Panasonic's 100th anniversary. Its idea is that a gathering of young energy, unbound by convention, will enrich the future a hundred years ahead. It is run by the general incorporated association 100BANCH, and the food space on the ground floor is operated by Cafe Company.

At its centre is the GARAGE Program. Every month, projects led by someone under 35 are selected through a review, and the chosen teams use the second-floor GARAGE free of charge. Around 10 to 20 project teams work on the same floor at any time, and the layout can be rearranged freely.
steps: 01 · 3F Loft
An event space for 100 people, with a 200-inch screen
The third-floor LOFT is an event space meant to spark encounters with new knowledge. It holds about 100 people and has a 200-inch screen and a wooden stage.

Workshops, screenings, concerts and even plays are held here. Because the stage sits right above the work floor, projects that grow on the second floor can step straight out in front of an audience upstairs.
3F Loft — a wooden stage and a large screen
Seating can be rearranged for each event
02 · 1F Kitchen
A test kitchen for the food of the future
The ground floor is a test kitchen run by Cafe Company. It explores future food experiences and works with 100BANCH projects as a place to create new value.
With food on the entrance floor, passers-by can feel the energy inside the building.
The food space run by Cafe Company

word.title: What is the GARAGE Program?
body: 100BANCH's accelerator for projects led by people under 35. Teams selected in the monthly review can use the second-floor GARAGE for free.
Instead of selling desks, it chooses projects and gives them space for free — the opposite entrance to an ordinary coworking space.

name: SHIBUYA QWS
card: About 2,600 m² devoted to questions, above the Scramble Crossing
title: SHIBUYA QWS — a 2,600 m² members' space on the 15th floor of Shibuya Scramble Square, built around asking questions
lead: SHIBUYA QWS (pronounced “Shibuya Cues”) is on the 15th floor of Shibuya Scramble Square's East Tower. The 2,600 m² floor holds PROJECT BASE with movable tables, the busy CROSS PARK, and SCRAMBLE HALL for 200 people. The official website describes it as a members' facility where diverse people cross paths and grow seeds of social value. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: QWS Project Member / Corporate & Public Member / QWS Commons / QWS Member
hero_cap: SCRAMBLE HALL — events right above the crossing
concept: Question with Sensibility — start with a question

The name QWS comes from “Question with Sensibility”. Ask the question before the answer, and let diverse people cross paths to grow seeds of social value — that is what this members' facility is for. Its academic partners include the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Science, Keio University, Waseda University, Tokyo Metropolitan University, Tokyo University of the Arts and Meiji University.

There are four kinds of members: QWS Project Members (teams of three or more), Corporate & Public Members for companies and local governments, QWS Commons who support as experts, and individual QWS Members. Through QWS Challenge, teams that pass a selection can use the project base for free.
steps: 01 · Scramble Hall
A 200-person hall overlooking the Scramble Crossing
SCRAMBLE HALL is an event space for about 200 people, looking down on Shibuya's famous Scramble Crossing. It has screens on three walls, sound, lighting and a green room.
The SALON has comfortable sofas and private rooms, used with restaurant service for business talks and for members to get to know each other.
SCRAMBLE HALL — events right above the crossing
SALON — sofas and private rooms for quiet conversation
02 · Playground and café
A running-track floor and a colourful café
PLAYGROUND is made for workshops. It has easy-to-move desks and chairs and screens that double as partitions, and its floor uses the same material as an athletics track.
CAFE HInT serves a colourful café menu. Besides three meeting rooms open to all members, there are private rooms by reservation.
PLAYGROUND — hands-on work on a running-track floor

word.title: What is QWS Challenge?
body: A selection programme run by SHIBUYA QWS. Projects that are chosen can use the project base free of charge.
Paying members and selected teams share the same floor. With one entrance for money and another for questions, the mix of people widens.

name: co-lab Shibuya Cast
card: A shared office for creators, running since 2003
title: co-lab Shibuya Cast — a 24-hour shared office for makers on the first two floors of Shibuya Cast
lead: co-lab Shibuya Cast occupies the first and second floors of Shibuya Cast at Shibuya 1-23-21. co-lab is a “shared office for creators that sparks collaboration”, run by Harumaki Project since 2003. Here there are 16 booths for 1–2 people, 7 studios for 3–5, 8 ateliers for 4–12 and 4 rooms for 12–22, all open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 4 rooms / 8 ateliers / 7 studios / 16 booths / 5 desks / flex
concept: Share of the Creative Life — when makers gather, the city changes

co-lab's motto is “when makers gather, the city changes”. It rests on three pillars: shared studios, a creative think tank it calls a “Do Tank”, and facilities that support making. It describes itself as a place that solves problems with collective intelligence gathered across organisations.

Shibuya Cast is a 17-storey building designed around the idea of “Echoes of Uniqueness”. co-lab Shibuya Cast, on its first two floors, is a creative platform that embodies “Share of the Creative Life” and supports the growth of the creative industries.
steps: 01 · 2F kitchen and shared areas
Window-side lounge and a kitchen
The second floor has a shared area along the windows and a kitchen — a place to work or rest outside your room.
Mail handling, high-speed internet, lockers and bicycle parking are available.
The second-floor kitchen
02 · 1F meeting rooms and workshop
Four meeting rooms and a place to make things
The ground floor has four meeting rooms, including the MR, which also works for workshops. There is also co-factory, equipment for making things, and an event space.
The eight ateliers for 4–12 people start at ¥160,000 a month, and the four rooms for 12–22 people at ¥380,000 a month (excluding tax).
The 1F MR, also used for workshops
Meeting room
Entrance to the ground-floor shared area
03 · The building
The lower floors of Shibuya Cast
Shibuya Cast is a 17-storey building at Shibuya 1-23-21, close to Shibuya Station.
Next door is the creative café “Are”, so the inside and outside of the building flow loosely together.
Shibuya Cast from outside

word.title: What is a Do Tank?
body: co-lab's word for a “creative think tank” that values actually making and running things, as opposed to a think tank that only thinks.
Bring outside problems into a shared office full of creators and solve them there. It does more than rent space — it turns the people gathered into work.

name: ARCH, Toranomon Hills
card: The first incubation center built only for corporate venture teams
title: ARCH — 3,800 m² on the 4th floor of Toranomon Hills Business Tower, built only for the new-business teams of large companies
lead: On the 4th floor of Toranomon Hills Business Tower, Mori Building runs ARCH, which it calls the world's first incubation center designed only for teams that create new businesses or transform existing ones inside large corporations. One 3,800 m² floor holds coworking areas, private offices, project rooms, a glass-walled event room and a café lounge. Everything below is based on the official website.
hero_cap: CO-WORK — choose your seat to suit the task
concept: Bringing the “outposts” of large companies under one roof

ARCH is for the teams inside large companies that build new businesses or drive change. Most incubators serve startups; ARCH focuses only on corporate venture teams, which its website describes as a world first. It is planned and run by Mori Building, with interiors by Wonderwall®.

The service rests on four pillars: training in the skills of building a business, mentoring by experienced mentors, networking across industries, and the 3,800 m² workplace itself. Two Chief Incubation Officers give advice and connect members with the right people.
steps: 01 · Co-work
Many kinds of seats, chosen to suit the task
CO-WORK offers a wide range of workspaces so members can pick where to work for each task. Every seat has power and network access.
PREMIUM CO-WORK is an executive area with its own lounge and private rooms.
CO-WORK — several kinds of seating
PREMIUM CO-WORK — quiet seats for executives
02 · Small office and project room
A second office, and rooms for short projects
SMALL OFFICE is a secure second office, also suited to new businesses run jointly by several companies.
PROJECT ROOM is a room for small teams that can be used for short-term projects — rent it only for the weeks you need to focus.
SMALL OFFICE — a lockable second office
PROJECT ROOM — for short, focused projects
03 · Magnet room and courtyard
A glass-walled event room and the courtyard beside it
MAGNET ROOM is an open, glass-walled space for seminars, events and workshops. Anyone outside can see what is happening inside.
Next to it, the COURTYARD is an open area with a pantry, used for events, seminars and lunch meetings.
MAGNET ROOM — events seen through the glass
COURTYARD — the open area next to the magnet room
04 · Café & lounge
An airy café and lounge
The café lounge is the place for a light meal and a quick meeting. Weekly mixers, small round-table talks and pitch events are held inside the center.
The members' community platform has personal profiles, a company list, project records and a discussion board.
CAFÉ & LOUNGE — for breaks and quick meetings

word.title: What is a corporate “dejima”?
body: In Japanese business, a dejima is a team set up a little apart from the parent company to build new businesses or drive change. The name comes from Dejima, the small artificial island in Nagasaki that was Japan's only window to the West for two centuries. ARCH gathers only these teams in one place.
When people facing the same challenges share a floor, finding someone to talk to becomes easy. Choosing carefully who to bring together is what gives the place its value.

name: LIFORK Otemachi
card: A calm, refined shared office directly connected to Otemachi Station
title: LIFORK Otemachi — a refined 24-hour shared office on the first two floors of Otemachi First Square, connected to the station
lead: LIFORK Otemachi, run by NTT Urban Development, is on the first and second floors of Otemachi First Square West Tower, directly connected to Otemachi Station. It has 13 types of shared office for 4 to 30 people, Style Rooms rented by the hour and a 199.1 m² rental lounge; the shared offices are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The official website describes “an open space with refined, calm interiors”. Everything below is based on the official website.
concept: A place to work for a better life

LIFORK is NTT Urban Development's brand of shared offices, rental spaces and coworking, under the banner “a place to work for a better life”. It has sites in Akihabara, Harajuku, Minami-Aoyama and Hisaya-odori in Nagoya; Otemachi is the one designed most for focused work.

The building, Otemachi First Square West Tower, connects directly to Otemachi Station (Tokyo Metro Tozai, Marunouchi, Chiyoda and Hanzomon lines, and Toei Mita line) through exits C8, C11 and C12. It is also a five-minute walk from the Marunouchi North Exit of JR Tokyo Station.
steps: 01 · Shared facilities
Lockers, smart locks and drinks
Members get lockers, smart-lock entry, self-service drinks, a pantry with a microwave, a multifunction printer and a business-card scanner.
With no physical key to carry, members can come and go on their own late at night and on holidays.
Member lockers
Self-service drinks
02 · Rental lounge
199.1 m², 50 seated or 60 standing
The rental lounge is 199.1 m² and holds up to 50 people seated or 60 standing. It has a 130-inch screen, a 65-inch monitor, wireless microphones and a projector.

It costs ¥44,000 per 60 minutes (¥40,000 before tax), with a 60-minute minimum and 15-minute increments after that. Hours are 9:00–21:00; other times on request. It is used for seminars, mixers, award ceremonies, photo shoots and screenings.
The rental lounge
03 · Style rooms
Ten rooms rented in 30-minute blocks
There are ten Style Rooms, B to L. Rooms for 4 cost ¥1,650 per 30 minutes, rooms for 8 cost ¥2,200 (¥1,925 for room C), and room G for 16 costs ¥4,400.
They are available 9:00–21:00, with a 30-minute minimum and 15-minute increments after that. Non-members can rent them by the room.
STYLE ROOM G, for 16 people

word.title: What is a smart lock?
body: An electronic lock opened with a smartphone or card instead of a physical key. LIFORK Otemachi uses one for member entry.
For a space open around the clock, managing who comes and goes when no one is at reception is the key question. A system that needs no keys handed out greatly reduces the work of running it.

credits: LIFORK official website: “LIFORK Otemachi”, “Share Office”, “Rental Lounge”, “Style Room”, “Access”

name: WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square
card: High floors directly above Shibuya Station, with 70 meeting rooms
title: WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square — floors 37–42 and 45 above Shibuya Station, with 70 meeting rooms
lead: WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square is in the East Tower of Shibuya Scramble Square, directly connected to Shibuya Station. It uses floors 37–42 and 45 of the 47-storey building (with 7 basement levels) and has 70 meeting rooms. Ceilings are 3,000–3,200 mm high. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 47 floors above ground, 7 below; East Tower opened November 2019
hero_cap: The window-side lounge, looking down on Shibuya
concept: A high-rise workplace right above the station

Shibuya Scramble Square's East Tower opened in November 2019. The 47-storey building connects directly to Shibuya Station, served by the JR Yamanote Line, Tokyu Toyoko and Den-en-toshi lines, Tokyo Metro Hanzomon and Fukutoshin lines, and the Keio Inokashira Line. WeWork occupies floors 37–42 and 45.
There are four plans: Private Office, Private Access, Dedicated Desk and All Access Plus. Reception is open 8:30–20:00 on weekdays. There are phone booths, a parent-and-child room and a café.
steps: 01 · 42F lounge
A long shared lounge along the windows
The 42nd-floor lounge runs along the windows, so you can work while looking down over Shibuya. It suits both solo work and quick chats.
With ceilings of 3,000–3,200 mm and high-rise windows, it rarely feels crowded.
The window-side lounge, looking down on Shibuya
02 · Meeting rooms
70 rooms across the building
There are 70 meeting rooms, from small huddle rooms to larger conference rooms.
Phone booths let you take online meetings away from your desk.
A meeting room, with the lounge visible through the glass
03 · Kitchen and events
A kitchen, and a lounge set up for events
The 42nd floor has a kitchen, and the lounge can be rearranged for events.
With a café on site, switching between work and breaks happens on the same floor.
The lounge arranged for an event

word.title: What is All Access?
body: A WeWork plan with no fixed desk or room: you use the shared spaces of multiple locations. The official site lists it as “All Access Plus”.
It suits people who do not work from one place. Make Shibuya your base and still sit down on the same terms in other parts of the city.

credits: WeWork Japan official website: “WeWork Shibuya Scramble Square”
